summary: Active Forest Service lookout on the Colville National Forest, with a 1961 flattop tower and a 1914 cabin that was the forest's first permanent lookout.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab on 20' timber tower
facts.status_note: staffing reportedly transitioned from Forest Service to volunteers in 2025 (Wikipedia; not corroborated by a second source)

access.note: reached via trail #306 after hiking to the mountain from several trailheads

events.note: lone watchman with tent shelter on the summit
12x12 ft log cabin with viewing platform, designed by Forest Supervisor C.C. Reed; first permanent lookout on the Colville National Forest
taller lookout with crow's-nest cab built alongside the 1914 cabin, used through 1960
current 15x15 ft R-6 flattop cab on 20 ft timber tower built (firelookout.com gives 1963)
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, February 5, 1996
Walker and Spur Mountain fires came close to the summit area
staffing said to have transitioned from Forest Service to volunteers

evidence.quote: The first lookout on Mount Bonaparte, circa 1904, was a solitary man keeping watch from the summit with a tent set for shelter.

evidence.supports: 1914 cabin, first permanent lookout, C.C. Reed design
evidence.quote: After ten years of temporary tent shelters for the fire watchers, a cabin with lookout platform was erected in 1914, one of several built in that year designed by Forest Supervisor CC Reed.
The second lookout was taller with the cabin at the top of the tower, and in service from 1930 through 1960.

evidence.supports: 1961 current tower, used until 2025 then volunteers
evidence.quote: In about 1961, the current lookout and its 20 ft (6.1 m) tall tower were installed, remaining in forest service control and use until 2025, when the staffing transitioned to volunteers.

evidence.supports: 1961 build date, staffed every summer, hip roof maintenance
evidence.quote: The present 20' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, built in 1961, is staffed every summer.
Known lookout personnel: 1923: Sidney Swain; 1929: B. Forrester; 1952: William Foote.
The present 15' x 15' R-6 flattop cab and catwalk on a 20' timber tower was built in 1963 and remains in active service.
The lookout area has been threatened by wildfires, with the 2021 Walker and Spur Mountain Fires coming very close to the summit area.

evidence.supports: 1914 cabin described as storage building, NHLR registration date Feb 5 1996
evidence.quote: Date Registered February 5, 1996 ... The first 12' x 12' flat-hewn tapered wall groundhouse with tower was constructed in 1914 and the house portion remains today as a storage building.

it has a square outline with a 12 ft x 12 ft (3.7 m x 3.7 m) base and a pyramidal outline sloping inwards at about 15 deg to the low roofline ... The tower remained in use through the 1920's before being transitioned to a storage shed after the lookout platform and top roof were removed in 1930.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1963 for the current tower; Wikipedia and firelookout.com both say 1961. Story notes the discrepancy and favors 1961 (two of three sources).

NHLR's own description text says summit use as a tent camp dates to 'as early as 1906', while Wikipedia gives 'circa 1904'. The story's 1904 claim is sourced to Wikipedia only; footnote corrected to [^2] rather than [^1] since NHLR's figure differs.

notes_for_editor: The claim that staffing shifted to volunteers in 2025 comes only from Wikipedia's prose (uncited inline) and should be verified against a Forest Service source before being treated as settled. Build year for the current tower (1961 vs 1963) is unresolved between NHLR and the other two sources.
